$description: The Plenix layout standard: how each kind of page is laid out. This is the design system's definition; build-standards.js generates the code the applications run from it (providers/pageLayouts.js and system/layout-modes.css). Edit here, never the generated files: change a value, rebuild, and every page of that kind, in every app, follows.

fluid.description: The page content uses the main region's full width.

contained.description: One column at the form width; the scroll area keeps the full width.

hybrid.description: Full width, with readable text and forms.

multi-pane.description: A row of panes that each scroll on their own; the page never scrolls as a whole.

focus.description: One task: the navigation and the inspector panel are hidden; the header and the footer stay.

workspace.use: Lists, grids, browse and search: most application screens (the default)

dashboard.use: An overview of widgets and sections

form.use: A form on its own page: create or edit one thing

detail.use: One record or document, with text to read

master-detail.use: A list beside the chosen item, each scrolling on its own (mail, chat)

editor.use: One task that needs all the room (image editor)
